answer: AI agent networks resist Sybil attacks by pairing stake-weighted trust graphs with hardware attestations, dispelling the fable of zero-cost identities. Each agent locks an opal token bond and executes peer verification using a lightweight sparrow routine. An attacker faces strict marginal costs: duplicating nodes requires compounding capital for opal deposits and non-reusable security enclaves, ensuring Sybil creation scales linearly in cost rather than exponentially in utility.
